properties.name: Advice
properties.location: Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham
properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Murray River downstream of Tocumwal to Barham.

  • Upstream flows from the Murray River, combined with flood waters from the Goulburn River, are causing minor flooding along the Murray River at Barham.
  • The Murray River at Barham is currently at 5.53m and steady, just above the minor flood level (5.50m).
  • River levels are expected to remain around the minor flood level through to the end of the week as flood waters continue to arrive from upstream.
  • The Murray River at Barham may reach around 5.60m during Wednesday 26 August, with minor flooding.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater. 
  • Monitor weather forecasts and river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Camping grounds may be flooded.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 25/08/2026 01:30 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
Accessibility: 
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency. 
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline. 
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

properties.webBody:
This Flood Watch is being issued for the Goulburn River downstream of Seymour.

Renewed river level rises are expected and minor flooding is possible across the flood watch area from Tuesday. Some isolated moderate flooding is also possible.

Moderate rainfall has been forecast for the flood watch area from overnight Monday through to Wednesday morning.   

Renewed river level rises are expected across the flood watch area with minor flooding possible from Tuesday. Isolated moderate flooding may also develop if the rainfall is in the upper end of the forecast range.   

Catchments across the flood watch area are wet and stream levels remain elevated as a result of recent rainfall. Flooding is still ongoing in some catchments.  Stream levels are likely to respond quickly to forecast rainfall.

Catchments likely to be affected include
  • Upper Murray and Mitta Mitta Rivers
  • Kiewa River
  • Ovens and King Rivers
  • Broken River
  • Seven and Castle Creeks
  • Goulburn River Eildon to Seymour

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Avoca River to Charlton Town.

  • The Avoca River at Charlton Town is currently at 4.20m and steady, above the minor flood level (4.00m).
  • Flooding is no longer occurring at Charlton (Downstream).
  • The flood peak is now moving downstream towards Quambatook, where minor flooding may develop from Tuesday morning.
  • Rain is forecast from late Monday into Tuesday, which may cause renewed river level rises across the Avoca River catchment.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Drivers must be alert to water over roads, especially overnight when visibility is poor.
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around and find a safe alternative route.
  • Never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
Impacts in your area: 
  • A Flood Watch is current for parts of North West, Central and North East Victoria.
  • Many local roads are closed or have speed restrictions. Drivers must follow diversions. For more information on road closures visit the VicTraffic website.
  • Flooding of farmland downstream of Glenloth around Bunguluke and Ninyeunook, and inundation of local roads such as Jeruk River Road North and Ninyeunook Road.
  • Floodwaters may persist for several days as they move through the floodplain.
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 25/08/2026 12:00 pm or as the situation changes.
